title: Quality, Quantity, And Strategy
paragraphs: “Everyone, are you okay? Wait—Sakura-chan, that’s a terrible wound!”

Father hurriedly rushed over to Sakura-chan and began treating her wounds. Then, turning back, he glared at the enemy. His gaze alone sent a clear message—if they made any sudden moves, he wouldn’t show mercy. The Dragon Emperor, the griffon, and that brat all froze under Father’s glare.
Naturally. If any of them were foolish enough to charge forward, they’d have to be complete idiots.
“Oh dear, how unfortunate.”
“Onii-chan!”
“Ta-Takt!”
“Takt.”
The brat, the Dragon Emperor, and the griffon all fell silent. Takt slowly emerged from behind the brat and walked between her and Father’s group.
“My, my. It seems my companions have been rather rude.”
“Takt! That thing in front of you is a Dragon Emperor and a Filolial! Hurry up and dispose of them!”
Takt cast a brief glance at the Dragon Emperor. In response, both the Dragon Emperor and the griffon instantly quieted down, and then he turned toward the brat.
“Onii-chan! They were bullying me!”
“Nana, what exactly happened?”
“That girl used her Filolial to attack me!”
“Lies! It was you who launched an attack without warning under the pretense of a duel! And when we started gaining the upper hand, those two behind you struck us with a sneak attack!”
Fiancée pointed angrily at the brat and shouted.
“Onii-chan, believe me! I’m not lying!”
But the brat simply shook her head and even put on a fake crying act while looking up at Takt.
Disgusting. Takt let out an exaggerated sigh and patted the brat’s head. At that moment, Father got the impression that this reaction meant he had chosen to believe her.
“Putting aside who’s right or wrong, I don’t think this is the place for a fight. Nana, you’re going to be a fine lady someday, aren’t you?”
“But… I’m not at fault.”
While scolding the brat, Takt then turned his gaze toward Father, eyeing him with an appraising look.
“Takt! That thing is a Filolial. I will not tolerate this!”
Noticing that the commotion was starting to draw a crowd, Takt forced a fake smile and quietly muttered something to his dragon and griffon subordinates, making them settle down.
“Hmm… If Takt says so…”
“Yeah.”
“Now then.”

With that, Takt turned his face toward Father. Since Father had been warned about him beforehand, he remained on guard. That, and given everything that had happened, there was no reason to let his guard down.
“It seems that in this commotion, I can’t fully determine the truth of my sister Nana’s claims, but it does appear that we were at fault for the Filolial getting injured.”
Even though the situation made everything perfectly clear, it was obvious that he was trying to brush aside his sister and subordinates’ interference as a separate issue.
Did he really think something like that would fly? Or perhaps he was planning to take Father’s weapon away?
“My apologies. It seems I got a little too worked up… But let me make this clear—I find it hard to believe that my sister would be the one to attack first.”
“That’s how you apologize? After injuring our comrades?”
Father replied in clear displeasure, while Takt observed him, as if assessing his worth. At that moment, the rival turned to Father and spoke.
“Naofumi, those guys are cowards!”
“What happened?”
“When they started losing, they attacked from the side! And when we had injured one of them, multiple people tried to finish them off!”
“That’s what she’s saying. How do you explain that?”
After listening to his rival’s words, Father directed a hostile glare toward Takt and questioned him.

“I had ordered my subordinates to protect my sister, and as a result, things turned out this way. However, don’t you think your Filolial is also poorly disciplined? Letting it roam freely despite the presence of dragons—this is what happens.”
“…That sounds like you’re just shifting the blame.”
“Come now, shifting the blame? I’m simply stating the obvious. Letting a Filolial roam freely in a place where strong dragons might be present—I’d say that’s your own fault.”
“…Then I’ll return those words right back to you. You’re also letting your dragons roam freely. If the roles were reversed, would you be saying the same thing?”
It was as if a switch had flipped inside Father—he glared sharply at Takt. Meanwhile, his rival, looking entranced, eagerly added to Fiancée’s statement.
“Naofumi is getting angry.”
“…Yeah.”
“…He’s so reliable!”
“That’s right.”
Hearing this, his rival’s assistant and the mole chimed in with agreement.
“You seem like a very honorable person. However, battle is about quality, quantity, and strategy. If you insist on fighting fair and square, you’ll lose battles that you could have won.”
“…I see. I’ll take that into consideration. I’ll make sure to remember those words.”
At that, Father seemed to have reached his limit—he sighed in exasperation and abandoned the conversation.
“Yes, you should remember them. It’s a crucial lesson for battle.”
“That’s right! And what’s with that attitude? My brother is a prestigious Seven Star Hero, you know—”
The brat started making a fuss, but Takt silenced her with a wave of his hand.
A Seven Star Hero is prestigious? Then we, the Four Holy Heroes, must be even more so.
“Now then, from what I can see, you must be the Shield Hero, one of the Four Cardinal Heroes, who reportedly arrived today?”
“Huh?”

Even the brat finally seemed to grasp the status of the person she was speaking to. Yes, on a global scale, when comparing the Four Cardinal Heroes and the Seven Star Heroes, the former holds more faith and status. In other words, no matter how famous Takt was as a Seven Star Hero, Father, as one of the Four Cardinal Heroes, was already in a superior position.
“Ah… I am Iwatani Naofumi, the Shield Hero of the Four Cardinal Heroes.”
“I see. No wonder you are unfamiliar with the common sense of this world.”

So basically, he was implying that since Father was summoned from another world and lacked knowledge of this world’s common sense, it was only natural that Sakura-chan ended up injured—it was her own fault.
Brushing everything aside as a matter of common sense… If I had been there, I would have killed him on the spot!
“That being said, I must admit that we do bear some responsibility as well…”
Takt then briskly approached Father, prompting both him and his rival to take a battle-ready stance. Since I had already explained the ability to steal sacred weapons, Father immediately spoke up.
“Don’t come any closer.”
“Nano!”
“I was merely intending to heal the injured Filolial on your side.”
He was trying to hide it behind polite words, but his condescending attitude was blatantly obvious.
Who does he think he is, saying he’ll ‘heal’ them?
“Big brother…”
The brat, as if deeply moved by his supposed defiance of authority, clasped her hands together in admiration. I don’t understand what she sees in him.
“Sorry, but I’ll have to decline. We can heal our own wounds.”
Father placed his hands on Sakura-chan and began chanting a healing spell.
“My apologies, then.”

With a deliberately exaggerated bow, Takt stepped back. By that time, a considerable number of people had gathered, having heard the commotion. I analyzed that Takt had likely realized he wouldn’t be able to launch an attack under these circumstances.

“Tonight, I shall invite you to a banquet as a gesture of apology. At that time, I will also explain the customs and rules of this country—of this world—as a way of making amends. I do hope you will attend.”

Father continued to glare at Takt. Meanwhile, Takt, with an exaggerated shrug, turned his back on him and quickly left, taking the brat and his two subordinates with him. However, Father heard it. As Takt glanced at the mole, he muttered in a low voice, “What terrible taste.” The one being spoken about lowered their head in dejection. And it was right around that moment that I arrived on the scene.
